samples.summary: Heading memory propagates to every sibling bullet on split, so un-bulleting a list started from a heading turns plain body items into headings
samples.evidence: `applySplitBlock` now keeps `after.headingLevel` when `newBlockType === 'list-item'` (block-helpers.ts:260-262), and `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:330-331) always uses `newType = 'list-item'` when splitting a list item. So: bullet a Heading 2 → Enter at end → the new, empty bullet also carries `headingLevel: 2` → the user types body text ("revenue up") in it. Selecting the whole list and toggling the bullet off (editor.ts:2869-2872 → `unlistedBlockType`) now converts EVERY item, including the pure body-text ones, into Heading 2. The memory should arguably only ride along on a mid-text split of the original bulleted heading, not onto freshly created empty siblings. The new test at test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:189-207 locks in exactly this propagation, so nothing catches it.

samples.summary: Enter/Backspace to exit a list started from a heading now leaves the caret in a Heading block instead of Normal text
samples.evidence: `splitBlock` (document.ts:303-306) and `deleteBackward` (document.ts:264-269) call `unlistedBlockType(block)` for an empty list item. Combined with the split propagation in block-helpers.ts:260, the *trailing* empty bullet of a list that was created by bulleting a heading also carries `headingLevel`, so the usual "press Enter twice to leave the list" gesture drops the user into an empty Heading N block; everything typed afterwards is heading-styled body text. Previously this always exited to `paragraph`.

samples.summary: DOCX-imported list items that carry a headingLevel are now silently promoted to headings when un-bulleted
samples.evidence: docx-importer.ts:242 sets `block.headingLevel` from the parsed paragraph style regardless of `blockType`, and `parseParagraph`/`docx-style-map` can return `blockType: 'list-item'` together with a heading level (numbered paragraph with a Heading style). `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:340) keys only on `headingLevel !== undefined`, not on "was bulleted from a heading in this session", so removing the bullet on such an imported item converts it into a heading the user never created. Levels 7-9 from Word are also passed through as `HeadingLevel` and only clamped downstream by `blockStyleId`.

samples.summary: The advertised bullet round trip is not lossless: custom block spacing on the heading is overwritten twice
samples.evidence: On heading→list-item, `blockStyleId` drops from `heading-N` to `normal` (named-styles.ts:99-113), so memory.ts:272-274 (and yorkie-doc-store.ts:1404-1408) run `materializeBlockSpacing`, replacing any user-set marginTop/marginBottom with the `normal` defaults; un-bulleting replaces them again with the heading defaults. The change claims the round trip "gives the heading back", but user spacing overrides on that block are destroyed by it.

samples.summary: No way to clear the remembered heading level while staying a list item
samples.evidence: `setBlockType(id,'list-item', opts)` unconditionally restores `prevHeadingLevel` (memory.ts:257-262, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1394-1395/1457-1458) and `opts` has no field to opt out. Once a heading is bulleted, the only way to get a plain bullet is paragraph→list-item (two ops); every list-item derived from it via split (block-helpers.ts:260) inherits the memory permanently. Combined with finding 1 this makes the sticky state unclearable from the UI.

finding.summary: Heading memory propagates to every sibling bullet on split, so un-bulleting a list started from a heading turns plain body items into headings
finding.evidence: `applySplitBlock` now keeps `after.headingLevel` when `newBlockType === 'list-item'` (block-helpers.ts:260-262), and `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:330-331) always uses `newType = 'list-item'` when splitting a list item. So: bullet a Heading 2 → Enter at end → the new, empty bullet also carries `headingLevel: 2` → the user types body text ("revenue up") in it. Selecting the whole list and toggling the bullet off (editor.ts:2869-2872 → `unlistedBlockType`) now converts EVERY item, including the pure body-text ones, into Heading 2. The memory should arguably only ride along on a mid-text split of the original bulleted heading, not onto freshly created empty siblings. The new test at test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:189-207 locks in exactly this propagation, so nothing catches it.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. applySplitBlock keeps `after.headingLevel` whenever `newBlockType === 'list-item'` (block-helpers.ts:260-262), with no offset condition, and Doc.splitBlock unconditionally sets `newType = 'list-item'` for a list item (document.ts:329-331) — unlike the heading/title/subtitle branch which only carries the type forward for a mid-text split (document.ts:332-337). The memory is seeded by MemDocStore.setBlockType (memory.ts:249-262) and nothing clears it when the user subsequently types body text into the new empty bullet. editor.toggleList then runs unlistedBlockType over every block in the selection (editor.ts:2866-2878), and unlistedBlockType converts any block with a defined headingLevel back to a heading (types.ts:337-344). Result: a bullet that only ever contained body text is silently converted to Heading 2 on un-bulleting — a real, reachable wrong-state/broken-invariant bug. The test at test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:174-191 asserts the end-of-text propagation, confirming nothing catches it. No guard makes the path unreachable, the code is present exactly as described, and the issue is logic/state correctness, not another lens.

finding.summary: Enter/Backspace to exit a list started from a heading now leaves the caret in a Heading block instead of Normal text
finding.evidence: `splitBlock` (document.ts:303-306) and `deleteBackward` (document.ts:264-269) call `unlistedBlockType(block)` for an empty list item. Combined with the split propagation in block-helpers.ts:260, the *trailing* empty bullet of a list that was created by bulleting a heading also carries `headingLevel`, so the usual "press Enter twice to leave the list" gesture drops the user into an empty Heading N block; everything typed afterwards is heading-styled body text. Previously this always exited to `paragraph`.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described (document.ts:263-270 and 301-307 route empty-list-item Enter/Backspace through unlistedBlockType; block-helpers.ts:256-262 propagates headingLevel to the split-off list item), but it is the deliberate, documented and test-asserted behavior of this repository, not a logic error. docs/design/docs/docs.md:166-176 specifies that both keyboard exits resolve through unlistedBlockType instead of hardcoding 'paragraph', and that splitting a non-empty bulleted heading copies the level to the new bullet 'so every bullet in the run restores its heading on exit — not just the first one'. test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:174-191 asserts precisely the sequence the finding calls a bug (split at end of bulleted heading, then Backspace on the new empty bullet -> heading, level 2), and 149-158 assert the Enter equivalent. There is no wrong condition, missing guard, crash, or data-loss path: headingLevel is real retained model state and the exit reproduces it faithfully. The objection is that these restore semantics are the wrong product/UX choice (list items render as normal text so the restored heading surprises the user) — a design-fit judgment owned by another lens, and one that contradicts the in-repo spec and tests rather than an implementation invariant. Out of scope for the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Splitting a bulleted heading drops the remembered `headingLevel`, so only the FIRST bullet honours the new heading-restoring Enter/Backspace exit
finding.evidence: The delta makes `splitBlock`/`deleteBackward` exit an empty list-item via `unlistedBlockType(block)` (document.ts:304, :267) with the comment "so Enter matches Backspace and the toggle". But the non-empty split path chooses `newType = 'list-item'` (document.ts:330-331) and `applySplitBlock` then does `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel` (block-helpers.ts:256-258); the Yorkie store does the same (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049 only copies headingLevel when `newBlockType === 'heading'`). Real flow: bullet a Heading 2, type text, press Enter → the new bullet has no `headingLevel`; press Enter again on that empty bullet → it exits to a *paragraph*, while the original bullet would have exited to Heading 2. The stated invariant ("a `list-item` retains the level of the heading it was made from", docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-128) is violated by the split, so the new exit is inconsistent from the second line onward.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence is misquoted. `applySplitBlock` does NOT drop `headingLevel` on a list-item split: packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:260 reads `if (newBlockType !== 'heading' && newBlockType !== 'list-item') { delete after.headingLevel; }`, with a comment (lines 256-259) explicitly stating the split hands the heading memory to the new bullet so more than the first bullet restores its heading via `unlistedBlockType`. The second cited site is also wrong: the path `packages/docs/src/store/yorkie-doc-store.ts` does not exist; the real file packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts preserves the level in both split branches — line 2052 `(newBlockType === 'heading' || newBlockType === 'list-item') && block.headingLevel !== undefined` for the empty-after path and line 2144 for the non-empty-after path. Every split call path reaches this preserving code: document.ts:328-337 selects `newType = 'list-item'` for a list-item split, and MemDocStore.splitBlock (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:226-231) delegates directly to `applySplitBlock`. The claimed repro (bullet a Heading 2, type, Enter, Enter on the new empty bullet exits to paragraph) therefore cannot occur — the new bullet carries `headingLevel`, and `unlistedBlockType` at document.ts:304 (Enter) and :267 (Backspace) restores the heading identically. The docs.md:117-128 invariant is satisfied, not violated.
